question: Properly adjusted seat head restraints:
choices: Are designed to prevent whiplash if hit from behind.
Both A and C
Should always be at a level even with the back of head.

question: The driver should drive with both hands on the steering wheel approximately in the:
choices: 9 o’clock and 3 o’clock positions
11 o’clock and 6 o’clock positions
7 o’clock and 5 o’clock positions

question: When adjusting the driver’s seat for best driving posture, set the seat in an upright position where your body is about how far from the steering wheel?
choices: 6 to 8 inches
10 to 12 inches
18 to 24 inches

question: A child in a child passenger restraint system (car seat) should:
choices: be facing the rear of the car if weighing less than 20 pounds and under 1 year old.
be facing forward if the child is one through three years old, and weighs more than 20 pounds,
A & B

question: The lap belt should be worn:
choices: at the abdomen for extra comfort .
above the pelvis so it doesn’t touch the top of the thighs.
by pregnant women below the abdomen and the shoulder belt above the belly.

question: The safest place for children 12 and under to ride in a vehicle equipped with air bags is:
choices: The front seat
The back seat
The bed of a pick-up truck

question: The sign at the right means:
choices: Slow down and yield to traffic on main road when merging.
Always come to a complete stop.
Give your turn signal and proceed into traffic at regular speed.

question: What does a traffic signal with a yellow left arrow indicate to the driver?
choices: Prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.
Protected left turn is about to end.
Both of the above.

question: The center of the roadway is marked with one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. If the broken yellow line is on the right of the solid yellow line (your side) it means:
choices: You are not allowed to pass in this area.
You are in a “passing zone” and it is safe to pass other vehicles if no oncoming traffic is present.
You are only allowed to make right turns in this area.

question: It is illegal to park:
choices: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

question: The two-second rule for following at a safe distance will hold true at:
choices: Speeds up to 30 m.p.h.
Any speed.
Speeds up to 55 m.p.h.

question: Which lane must you be in before making a left turn from a one-way street?
choices: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

question: Motorists are required by law when passing a bicycle traveling in the same direction to allow a minimum distance of:
choices: 1 foot
3 feet
Safely away from the bicycle.

question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:
choices: Stop, check for cars and enter when safe.
Check for cars, reduce speed to 25 MPH before entering traffic lane.
Check for cars, increase your speed to match the flow of traffic and merge when the way is clear.

question: Emergency crossovers on the interstate are legal in Tennessee for:
choices: Making a U-Turn when you missed your exit.
Turning around when no others are present.
Emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews only.

question: Interstate driving demands require the driver to:
choices: Have a complete awareness of higher speed driving
Constant alertness by the driver
Both of the above.

question: Continuous hard braking on ice and snow often:
choices: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels causing the loss of steering control.
Keeps the brakes hot and prevents them from freezing.

question: When driving in foggy conditions, do not put your headlights on high beam because:
choices: The light from the fog creates blurry vision on your eyes.
Approaching vehicles won’t be able to see your oncoming vehicle.
Low beams provide greater visibility and you can be better seen by other vehicles.

question: Driving at night is:
choices: Safer because of less traffic and less distractions.
More hazardous because your range of visibility is limited by your headlights.
Safer and allows you to increase your speed while adjusting to road conditions.

question: Driving while under the influence of drugs carries:
choices: The same penalty as for alcohol
A lesser penalty than for alcohol.
Absolutely no penalty at all.

question: If you have had three beers in the past hour, about how long will it take for all the alcohol to leave your blood stream?
choices: One hour
Two hours
Three hours

question: As the percentage of alcohol (BAC) in your blood increases, you become:
choices: More intoxicated
More sober
More coordinated

question: Implied Consent Law means:
choices: If asked, you will take a test to determine alcohol or drug content in the blood.
The laws apply even without any signs, markings or signals present at an intersection.
The owner of the vehicle will carry proper insurance.

question: Which of the following driving skills are affected by the use of alcohol and/or drugs?
choices: Alertness and concentration
Reaction time and coordination
All of the above are affected.

question: If involved in a reportable accident, the operator of the vehicle must file an accident report to the Department of Safety within:
choices: 10 Days
20 Days
48 Hours

question: If you are not the first at the scene of accident and your help is not needed, what should you do:
choices: Slow down to calm your nerves.
Stop and look for your own curiosity.
Drive on and do not interfere with procedures.

question: A driver license may be revoked or suspended for:
choices: Frequent convictions of traffic law violations resulting in 12 or more “points” within a 12 month period
Fraudulently altering a driver license
Both of the above

question: A plastic shatter-resistant face shield:
choices: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Helps protect your whole face.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

question: More than half of all crashes:
choices: Occur at speeds greater than 35mph.
Happen at night.
Are caused by worn tires.
Involve riders who have less than five months of experience on their motorcycles.

question: When riding, you should:
choices: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look where you are going.

question: Usually, a good way to handle tailgaters is to:
choices: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.
Ignore them.

question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:
choices: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Cover the clutch lever and the brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

question: Making eye contact with other drivers:
choices: Is a good sign they see you.
Is not worth the effort it takes.
Doesn’t mean that the driver will yield.
Guarantees that the other driver will yield to you.

question: Reflective clothing should:
choices: Be worn at night.
Be worn during the day.
Not be worn.
Be worn day and night

question: The best way to stop quickly is to:
choices: Use the front brake only.
Use the rear brake first.
Throttle down and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

question: When it starts to rain it is usually best to:
choices: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble:
choices: Accelerate out of the wobble.
Use the brakes gradually.
Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.
Downshift.

question: If you are chased by a dog:
choices: Kick it away.
Stop until the animal loses interest.
Swerve around the animal.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

question: Passengers should:
choices: Lean as you lean.
Hold on to the motorcycle seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto you.

question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:
choices: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the tail end of the group.
Beside the leader.

question: If you wait one hour per drink for the alcohol to be eliminated from your body before riding:
choices: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Side effects from the drinking may still remain.
You will be okay as long as you ride slowly.

question: It is MOST important to flash your brake light when:
choices: Someone is following too closely.
You will be slowing suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.
Your signals are not working.

question: The FRONT brake supplies how much of the potential stopping power?
choices: About 25%.
About 50%.
At least 70%.
All of the stopping power.

question: To swerve correctly:
choices: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, it is usually best to:
choices: Relax on the handgrips.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

question: The car below is waiting to enter the intersection. It is best to:
choices: Make eye contact with the driver.
Reduce speed and be ready to react.
Maintain speed and position.
Maintain speed and move right.
